name: Text skeleton
summary: An article that shows grey lines of its own shape while it loads, then fills in with no jump: title, byline and paragraphs keep their size.
use: for reading content (an article, a note, a help page) that takes longer than about a second to load
a11y: While loading, the content area is aria-busy and inert, so nobody can tab into placeholders; a polite status says when loading starts and when it is done. Under reduced motion the bones stay still.
notes: Delete the button marked data-odl-demo; set aria-busy on .odl-body from your own request.

use_when: text content loads after the page frame, and the wait is usually over 1 second
avoid_when: the wait is under about 300 ms: show nothing
an action the person started (saving, sending): use inline-spinner
a long task with steps: use progress-steps

parts.name: title
parts.what: the heading: what happened, in plain words, as in “Set up approval rules”

parts.name: byline
parts.what: the date and reading time, as in “Updated Nov 10 · 4 minute read”

parts.name: body
parts.what: the article text, as in “Approval rules decide who signs off on a bill be”

empty.how: When the request returns nothing, replace the bones with an empty state (empty-first-use or empty-no-results).

loading.how: aria-busy turns each text run, picture and control into a bone of its own size; nothing moves when data arrives.

error.how: When the request fails, keep the frame and show an error banner with a retry (page-banners) in place of the rows.

disabled.how: While loading, the content is inert, so placeholders can't be focused or clicked.

overflow.how: Single lines end in an ellipsis, so a long value never adds a line or moves the next row.

long_text.how: Each line is clamped to one line with an ellipsis, so the skeleton and the loaded layout keep one height.

keyboard: Tab reaches Show loaded (the demo toggle), then the loaded content once it's ready; nothing inside is focusable while loading
